title: Make the app installable as a PWA with a network-first service worker
context: The app needed to be installable as a PWA. The service worker comment also says the window should open even while the local server is starting. The commit adds a web manifest, icons, and a service worker, and registers the worker only in production builds.
decision: Add public/manifest.json (standalone display, #667eea theme, two icons) and public/sw.js, a minimal network-first service worker. src/index.js registers /sw.js on window load, only when NODE_ENV is production. The worker caches same-origin GET responses and falls back to cache when the network fails. Requests under /api/ and /socket.io/ are passed through uncached.
consequences: Online requests always go to the network first, so a rebuilt app is picked up on the next load; the cache is used only when the fetch fails.
The worker calls skipWaiting and clients.claim, so a new worker activates immediately and deletes old caches whose names differ from transcriber-shell-v1.
Offline navigation falls back to the cached '/' page; other offline requests with no cache entry get Response.error().
The worker is not registered in development builds, so PWA behavior can only be exercised in production.
The code excludes only /api/ and /socket.io/. The sw.js comment says audio requests are also never touched, but no audio path is excluded in the shown code, so same-origin audio GETs would be cached.
Google Fonts is linked from index.html, but the worker ignores cross-origin requests, so the font is not cached for offline use.
index.html also changes the theme color to #667eea and the title to 'Meeting Transcriber'.
